- For N = 1, N₀ = 0, d = 4 and S = {0}: the sum is 1.

- For N = 1, N₀ = 0, d = 4 and S = {1}: the sum is 0 (an odd part cannot have even total).

- S = ∅ gives 0.

- N = 1, N₀ = 0, S = {0}, d = 4: Σ_stable(4) = 1.


<a id="moment-minus-component-profile-vanishes"></a>


**Moment minus component profile vanishes.** In [whole fixed degree component profile](#whole-fixed-degree-component-profile), let B_n bound the total number of geometric components (uniformly in q) and K_d be the uniform component error of Wood Theorem 4.7. Then |Ẽ_n^±(q)/M(q) − P_n^±(q)| ≤ B_n(K_d q^{−1/2} + q^{−1})/(1 − q^{−1}); in particular the difference is O_n(q^{−1/2}). One may take B_n = D_d, the degree of the finite étale map CHur_{F,d} → Conf_d.

Throughout this assertion, as in [whole fixed degree component profile](#whole-fixed-degree-component-profile) B_n a q-uniform bound on the number of geometric components


To prove the assertion, A rational point lies on a Frobenius-fixed component; non-fixed open and closed components contribute no F_q-points. Each fixed component C has |#C(F_q) − q^d| ≤ K_d q^{d−1/2} (Theorem 4.7, IG.5; the marked-cover comparison); the rigid moment numerator is Σ_C #C(F_q) (Proposition 4.4, IG.4). The denominator is q^d(1 − q^{−1}) ([imaginary exact slice parametrization](#imaginary-exact-slice-parametrization), [real exact slice parametrization](#real-exact-slice-parametrization)); divide by it and by M(q) ≥ 1, using C_n(q) ≤ B_n. B_n = D_d is q-independent because the degree of CHur_{F,d} → Conf_d is constant over the connected base (IG.5; the marked-cover comparison).

*Needs:* [whole fixed degree component profile](#whole-fixed-degree-component-profile), [imaginary exact slice parametrization](#imaginary-exact-slice-parametrization), [real exact slice parametrization](#real-exact-slice-parametrization), InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4, InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5.

([[50]](#ref-50), Theorem 4.7, p.21 (arXiv v2; Duke 168, p.404–405).)


**Checks.**


- If no component is fixed, the moment is O_n(q^{−1/2}).

- The bound is uniform in q at fixed n only.


<a id="ordinary-limit-iff-eventual-profile-constancy"></a>


**Ordinary limit iff eventual profile constancy.** Under [moment minus component profile vanishes](#moment-minus-component-profile-vanishes) (with M(q) ≤ K uniformly, as M(q) divides |H₂(F, c)|), the limit of Ẽ_n^±(q)/M(q) as q → ∞ along allowed prime powers exists iff P_n^±(q) is eventually equal to a single rational value, and then that value is the limit. This is a criterion, not a proof that every bad type satisfies it.

Throughout this assertion, as in [moment minus component profile vanishes](#moment-minus-component-profile-vanishes) M(q) ≤ K := |H₂(F, c)| for all q


To prove the assertion, The profile takes values in the finite set {a/b : 0 ≤ a ≤ B_n, 1 ≤ b ≤ K} (API profile_mem_finite). By [moment minus component profile vanishes](#moment-minus-component-profile-vanishes) the moment converges iff the profile converges, to the same limit. A convergent function with values in a finite subset of R is eventually constant: a finite subset of a T1 space is discrete (Mathlib Finite.instDiscreteTopology) and convergence to a point of a discrete subtype is eventual equality (Mathlib Filter.tendsto_pure).

*Needs:* [moment minus component profile vanishes](#moment-minus-component-profile-vanishes), [whole fixed degree component profile](#whole-fixed-degree-component-profile), `Finite.instDiscreteTopology` (Mathlib), `Filter.tendsto_pure` (Mathlib).

([[50]](#ref-50), Proof of Theorem 1.2, p.23 (arXiv v2; Duke 168, p.407).)


**Checks.**


- Constant profile: the limit exists.

- Profile alternating between two values: no limit, even though the liminf bound may hold.


<a id="liminf-limsup-from-recurrent-profile-values"></a>


**Liminf limsup from recurrent profile values.** Under [moment minus component profile vanishes](#moment-minus-component-profile-vanishes), let R_n^± be the set of profile values attained for arbitrarily large allowed q. It is a nonempty finite set, and liminf_q Ẽ_n^±(q)/M(q) = min R_n^±, limsup_q Ẽ_n^±(q)/M(q) = max R_n^±. In particular the bad-type bound of [bad type lower bound](#bad-type-lower-bound) bounds every recurrent value from below.

Throughout this assertion, as in [moment minus component profile vanishes](#moment-minus-component-profile-vanishes)


To prove the assertion, Finitely many profile values occur (API profile_mem_finite); discard those taken only for boundedly many q; the remaining set is nonempty. Along an unbounded sequence of q with profile value r, the moment tends to r (error O(q^{−1/2})); conversely every limit point of the moment is a limit point of the profile, hence in R_n^±.

*Needs:* [moment minus component profile vanishes](#moment-minus-component-profile-vanishes), [whole fixed degree component profile](#whole-fixed-degree-component-profile), [bad type lower bound](#bad-type-lower-bound), `Filter.limsup` (Mathlib).

<a id="weight-polynomial-formula-for-the-stable-orthant"></a>


**Weight polynomial formula for the stable orthant.** In [complete stable range component sum](#complete-stable-range-component-sum), let δ ≡ N₀ (mod 2), 1 = (1, …, 1), and W(X) := Σ_{ε ∈ S} X^{wt(ε + δ·1)} (the weight enumerator of the surviving parities shifted by N₀). Then, as formal power series, Σ_{d ≥ 0} Σ_stable(d) X^d = X^{N·N₀} W(X)/(1 − X²)^N, equivalently (1 − X²)^N · Σ_d Σ_stable(d) X^d = X^{N N₀} W(X).

Throughout this assertion, as in [complete stable range component sum](#complete-stable-range-component-sum)


To prove the assertion, For a fixed ε the least allowed coordinate is N₀ + ((ε_i − N₀) mod 2), and the other allowed values add 2z_i, z_i ≥ 0: the generating series of the parity class is X^{N N₀ + wt(ε + δ·1)}/(1 − X²)^N. Sum over ε ∈ S; the coefficient identity is [stable parity multidegree count](#stable-parity-multidegree-count) (stars and bars). No analytic convergence is used.

*Needs:* [complete stable range component sum](#complete-stable-range-component-sum), [stable parity multidegree count](#stable-parity-multidegree-count), `PowerSeries` (Mathlib).

**Checks.**

### 5.22 Semidirect products and function-field moments


<a id="surjections-onto-a-semidirect-product"></a>


**Surjections onto a semidirect product.** Let Γ be a finite group, H a finite Γ-group and G a profinite group. There is a bijection between Sur(G, H ⋊ Γ) (continuous surjections) and tuples (ρ, N, s, φ) with ρ ∈ Sur(G, Γ), N ⊆ ker ρ a closed normal subgroup of G, s : Γ → G/N a homomorphic section of the induced map ρ : G/N → Γ, and φ : ker ρ/N → H a Γ-isomorphism, where Γ acts on ker ρ/N through s and conjugation. The bijection sends ψ to (projection of ψ to Γ, ker ψ, ψ^{−1} restricted to Γ, ψ|_{ker ρ/N}).

Throughout this assertion, Γ and H are finite, with discrete topologies; H carries the specified Γ-action. G profinite; homomorphisms continuous, N closed


To prove the assertion, Forward map as stated; ψ^{−1}(Γ) makes sense on G/N ≅ H ⋊ Γ. Inverse: from 1 → ker ρ/N → G/N → Γ → 1 and the section s get G/N ≅ ker ρ/N ⋊ Γ; extend φ to ker ρ/N ⋊ Γ ≅ H ⋊ Γ (Mathlib SemidirectProduct and its universal properties) and compose with G → G/N. Since N is closed and G/N is compact and finite, it is discrete. Thus the resulting algebraic isomorphisms and section are continuous, as required. The two constructions are mutually inverse (direct check).

*Needs:* `SemidirectProduct` (Mathlib), `SemidirectProduct.rightHom` (Mathlib), `SemidirectProduct.inr` (Mathlib).

([[51]](#ref-51), Lemma 9.1, p.37 (arXiv v2).)


**Checks.**


- H = 1: surjections G → Γ correspond to (ρ, ker ρ, the unique section, the unique map).

- Γ = 1: Sur(G, H) ↔ (N, φ) with φ : G/N ≅ H.


<a id="complements-of-a-coprime-abelian-normal-subgroup-are-conjugate"></a>


**Complements of a coprime abelian normal subgroup are conjugate.** Let E be a finite group and H ⊴ E an abelian normal subgroup with gcd(|H|, [E : H]) = 1. Then H has a complement in E and any two complements are conjugate by an element of H. Consequently, for Γ finite and H a finite abelian Γ-group with gcd(|H|, |Γ|) = 1, the sections of H ⋊ Γ → Γ form one H-conjugacy orbit, and there are exactly [H : H^Γ] of them.

Throughout this assertion, E finite; H abelian normal; |H| and [E : H] coprime


To prove the assertion, Existence is Mathlib's Schur–Zassenhaus theorem (Subgroup.exists_right_complement'_of_coprime). Two complements K, K' ≅ Γ := E/H give a 1-cocycle c : Γ → H with k' = c(γ)k; H¹(Γ, H) is killed by |Γ| (corestriction–restriction) and by |H|, hence is 0 when they are coprime, so c is a coboundary c(γ) = hγ(h)^{−1} and K' = h K h^{−1}. Sections of H ⋊ Γ → Γ correspond to complements; H acts on them by conjugation transitively, with stabiliser of the standard section Γ equal to H^Γ.

*Needs:* `Subgroup.exists_right_complement'_of_coprime` (Mathlib), `SemidirectProduct` (Mathlib).

([[51]](#ref-51), Proof of Lemma 9.3, p.39 (arXiv v2).)


**Checks.**


- H = 1: one section.

- Γ = Z/2 acting by −1 on H = Z/3: [H : H^Γ] = 3 sections, the three involutions' subgroups of S_3.


<a id="counting-unramified-h-extensions-via-semidirect-extensions"></a>


**Counting unramified h extensions via semidirect extensions.** Let Γ be finite, Q = Q or F_q(t), and H a finite Γ-group with gcd(|H|, |Γ|) = 1 such that (SZ) all sections of H ⋊ Γ → Γ are H-conjugate (true when H is abelian: [complements of a coprime abelian normal subgroup are conjugate](#complements-of-a-coprime-abelian-normal-subgroup-are-conjugate)). Let N(H, Γ, D, Q) be the number of surjections Gal(Q̄/Q) → H ⋊ Γ whose H ⋊ Γ-extension K has rDisc K = D, whose H-extension K/K^H is unramified everywhere and split completely above ∞, and whose Γ-extension K^H/Q is split completely at ∞. Then Σ_ρ |Sur_Γ(Gal(K_ρ^{un,∞}/K_ρ)^{(|Γ|′)}, H)| = [H : H^Γ]^{−1} N(H, Γ, D, Q), where ρ runs over surjections Gal(Q̄/Q) → Γ split completely at ∞ with rDisc = D (Γ-extensions with their identification, not isomorphism classes) and the Γ-action is that of the chosen section on the maximal pro-|Γ|′ quotient. Summing instead over isomorphism classes E_Γ(D, Q), the right side acquires the factor |Z(Γ)|/|Γ|.

Throughout this assertion, Γ finite; H finite Γ-group with gcd(|H|, |Γ|) = 1 (SZ): sections of H ⋊ Γ → Γ are H-conjugate left side summed over surjections ρ (see the correction for isomorphism classes)


To prove the assertion, Apply [surjections onto a semidirect product](#surjections-onto-a-semidirect-product) with G = Gal(Q̄/Q). For each ρ, the maximal pro-|Γ|′ quotient ker ρ/M carries a distinguished section s_ρ (LWZB Definition 2.1); tuples with s = s_ρ correspond to Γ-surjections ker ρ/M → H; the local conditions and rDisc = D match on both sides. By (SZ), all sections of G/N → Γ are ker ρ/N-conjugate with stabiliser (ker ρ/N)^Γ, so there are [H : H^Γ] sections, each with the same number of φ's.

*Needs:* [surjections onto a semidirect product](#surjections-onto-a-semidirect-product), [complements of a coprime abelian normal subgroup are conjugate](#complements-of-a-coprime-abelian-normal-subgroup-are-conjugate), InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4.

([[51]](#ref-51), Lemma 9.3, p.38 (arXiv v2); [[51]](#ref-51), Introduction, p.3 (arXiv v2).)


**Checks.**


- H = 1: each isomorphism class of S_3-extensions with its Γ-action gives exactly |Inn(S_3)| = 6 surjections, so N(1,S_3,D,Q) = 6·#E_{S_3}(D,Q). There is at least one totally real example at D = 229: the splitting field of x³ − 4x + 1, an irreducible cubic with positive nonsquare discriminant 229. No uniqueness of that field is needed.

- The moment ratios of Theorem 1.4 are unchanged by the normalisation.


<a id="liu-wood-zureick-brown-function-field-moments"></a>


**Liu wood zureick brown function field moments.** Let Γ be finite and H a finite admissible Γ-group satisfying (SZ). For prime powers q with gcd(q, |Γ||H|) = 1 and gcd(q − 1, |H|) = 1 put R_b(q) := Σ_{n ≤ b} Σ_{K ∈ E_Γ(q^n, F_q(t))} |Sur_Γ(Gal(K^#/K), H)| / Σ_{n ≤ b} |E_Γ(q^n, F_q(t))|, where E_Γ(D, F_q(t)) is the set of Γ-extensions of F_q(t) split completely at ∞ with radical discriminant norm D and K^# is the maximal unramified extension of K split completely above ∞ with all finite subextensions of degree prime to q(q − 1)|Γ|. Then lim_{b→∞} limsup_{q→∞} R_b(q) = lim_{b→∞} liminf_{q→∞} R_b(q) = [H : H^Γ]^{−1}. For every sufficiently large b, every limit point of R_b(q) in q lies within O_G(1/b) of [H : H^Γ]^{−1}; the existence of lim_{q→∞} R_b(q) is not proved.

Throughout this assertion, Γ finite; H finite admissible Γ-group; (SZ) q prime power, gcd(q, |Γ||H|) = 1, gcd(q − 1, |H|) = 1 (these force |H| odd)


To prove the assertion, Write a_Γ=|Z(Γ)|/|Γ|. The numerator over isomorphism classes is a_Γ[H:H^Γ]⁻¹ Σ_{n≤b}N(H,Γ,q^n,F_q(t)), while the denominator is a_Γ Σ_{n≤b}N(1,Γ,q^n,F_q(t)). Thus a_Γ cancels in the ratio. The Γ-surjections to H factor through Gal(K^#/K), since |H| is prime to q(q−1)|Γ|. N(H, Γ, q^n, F_q(t)) = #Hur^n_{G,c}(F_q) with G = H ⋊ Γ and c the nonidentity elements of the order of their image in Γ; after cancellation, the denominator is Σ_n #Hur^n_{Γ,Γ∖1}(F_q) (LWZB Lemma 10.2, IG.5). If Γ=1, admissibility forces H=1 and the ratio is identically 1, using the unique trivial extension of radical discriminant 1. Otherwise fix an allowed residue a of q modulo |G|² and replace b by b_a, the largest integer ≤b whose residue lies in E_a modulo M_a from Theorem 10.4. The omitted slices have no rational points. Since E_a is nonempty, 0≤b−b_a<M_a; for sufficiently large b this gives b_a≍b, uniformly over the finitely many a. Apply all following top-degree and error estimates at b_a, not at an empty degree-b slice. Grothendieck–Lefschetz (SF.2), Deligne's bound (DWP.7) and the Betti comparison (LWZB Lemma 10.3, IG.5) give |#Hur^b(F_q) − π(q, b) q^b| ≤ B(b) Σ_{j<2b} q^{j/2}, with the top-degree trace counting Frobenius-fixed components ([top cohomology counts rational components](#top-cohomology-counts-rational-components)); lower n contribute O_b(q^{b−1/2}). LWZB Theorem 10.4 (IG.5): π_{G,c}(q, b) = π_Γ(q, b) + O_G(b^{d_Γ(q)−2}) and π_Γ(q, b) ≥ C_G b^{d_Γ(q)−1} on the residues where it is nonzero; so R_b(q) = [H : H^Γ]^{−1}(1 + O_G(b^{−1}) + O_b(q^{−1/2})) along each residue class of q mod |G|², hence every limit point in q lies in [H : H^Γ]^{−1}(1 + O_G(1/b)).

*Needs:* [counting unramified h extensions via semidirect extensions](#counting-unramified-h-extensions-via-semidirect-extensions), [top cohomology counts rational components](#top-cohomology-counts-rational-components), InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2, DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7.

([[51]](#ref-51), Theorem 1.4, p.3 (arXiv v2); [[51]](#ref-51), Proof of Theorem 1.4, p.41 (arXiv v2).)


**Checks.**


- Γ = Z/2, H = Z/3 with inversion: [H : H^Γ]^{−1} = 1/3, the real-quadratic Cohen–Lenstra 3-moment, in the q → ∞ mode.

- Even |H| is excluded by the hypotheses (q or q − 1 is even).


<a id="cohen-lenstra-martinet-moments-over-function-fields"></a>


**Cohen lenstra martinet moments over function fields.** Let Γ be finite and H a finite abelian Γ-group with gcd(|H|, |Γ|) = 1 and H^Γ = 1. Then with q running over prime powers with gcd(q, |Γ||H|) = 1 and gcd(q − 1, |H|) = 1, lim_{b→∞} limsup_q and lim_{b→∞} liminf_q of Σ_{n ≤ b} Σ_{K ∈ E_Γ(q^n, F_q(t))} |Sur_Γ(Cl(O_K), H)| / Σ_{n ≤ b} |E_Γ(q^n, F_q(t))| both equal |H|^{−1}.

Throughout this assertion, Γ finite; H finite abelian Γ-group, gcd(|H|, |Γ|) = 1, H^Γ = 1 q as in [liu wood zureick brown function field moments](#liu-wood-zureick-brown-function-field-moments)


To prove the assertion, An abelian Γ-group is admissible iff gcd(|H|, |Γ|) = 1 and H^Γ = 1 (LWZB §7.1); (SZ) holds by [complements of a coprime abelian normal subgroup are conjugate](#complements-of-a-coprime-abelian-normal-subgroup-are-conjugate). By class field theory for function fields ([function-field class-field and Picard comparison](#support-function-fields)), Gal(K^#/K)^{ab} is the prime-to-q(q − 1)|Γ| part of Cl(O_K), so Γ-surjections onto the abelian H coincide. Apply [liu wood zureick brown function field moments](#liu-wood-zureick-brown-function-field-moments): [H : H^Γ]^{−1} = |H|^{−1}.

*Needs:* [liu wood zureick brown function field moments](#liu-wood-zureick-brown-function-field-moments), [complements of a coprime abelian normal subgroup are conjugate](#complements-of-a-coprime-abelian-normal-subgroup-are-conjugate), [function-field class-field and Picard comparison](#support-function-fields).

### 5.23 Locally compact quadratic spaces


<a id="refinement-lc-quadratic"></a>


**Lc quadratic.** For a locally compact Hausdorff topological abelian group V, a continuous QuadraticMap ℤ V (ℝ/ℤ) q has a polar adjoint V ≃ₜ+ Hom_cont(V,ℝ/ℤ), with compact-open topology; its value on (x,y) is q(x+y)−q(x)−q(y). Store this homeomorphic additive equivalence, not just injectivity. Second countability is imposed on the measure theorem, not on the carrier.

Throughout this assertion, V is locally compact, Hausdorff and a topological abelian group.

### 5.24 Locally compact maximal isotropics

Its probability topology is supplied by finite quotient reductions; it is not the discrete topology on a countable list of subgroup names.

### Supporting probability and arithmetic comparisons

<a id="support-quadratic-probability"></a>

For a second-countable weakly metabolic locally compact quadratic group, prove that the compact-open quadratic-isotropic reductions form a countable cofinal inverse system, that maximal-isotropic reductions compose and that the inverse-limit topology is the specified Borel structure. Use compatible finite uniform laws to obtain a unique Borel probability; prove continuous isometry invariance, almost-sure discreteness and finiteness of intersection with the fixed compact-open maximal isotropic. Infinite F_p-dimension gives the limiting Poonen–Rains law, while finite dimension gives its finite intersection law. Source: Poonen–Rains Theorem 2.19, pp. 9–11. The countable projective-measure extension is imported from Mathlib; the quadratic finite reductions and their compatibility are proved here.

For the arithmetic intersection prove the finite-flat theta obstruction and its local invariant normalization, with polar pairing the *negative* Weil-cup product and no division by two. Use global duality to identify the global image and local Kummer image as maximal isotropics and obtain `Sel_λ/Sha¹(k,A[λ])≃Z∩W`. Prove the finite-module Sha1 vanishing criteria separately from any assertion on Sha(A). Characteristic dividing the isogeny degree uses fppf cohomology throughout. Source: Poonen–Rains Proposition 3.3, Corollary 4.6 and Theorem 4.13, pp. 13–21; A3 and D7 supply the theta and duality machinery.

For integral quadratic models construct the smooth projective split orthogonal Grassmannian over Z and prove its finite reduction counts and component parity, including p=2. Oesterlé–Serre measure counts the liftable reduction image. In the smooth proper nonempty case the mass is `#X(F_p)p^-d`, and each reduction fibre has `p^d` lifts; the probability mass of a cylinder is its finite relative cardinality. Fixed-rank intersections use the intrinsic measure of their Schubert stratum, not conditioning on an ambient zero-probability rank-r event. Source: BKLPR Proposition 2.1, Corollary 2.2, Propositions 4.4–4.9 and §5.1, pp. 5–6 and 12–15.

For the all-prime symplectic model prove the primewise error bound and apply Borel–Cantelli: positive rank has summable nontrivial-primary probabilities, while rank zero has a divergent harmonic tail and yields an almost-sure infinite direct sum. The bounded-order rank-zero group-weight averages use the reciprocal finite product in the harmonic weight identity. They are not a probability on finite groups over all primes. Source: BKLPR Theorems 5.15–5.16 and Lemma 5.17, pp. 21–24.

<a id="support-cm"></a>

For CM twists retain the arithmetic CM action: maximal-order CM, all endomorphisms defined over the stated base, and the existence of a twist with good reduction. Then prove the local three-isogeny Tamagawa ratio and differential comparison at every place, including two and three. For nonmaximal orders pass through a base-defined isogeny and use corank invariance, rather than assert that geometric CM alone forces every local ratio one. At j=0 and 1728 use the appropriate larger twist automorphism group; the ordinary squareclass-injectivity assertion excludes them or records its fibre. Sources: Rubin's CM lemmas as used in BKLOS §12, and BKLOS Theorems 2.1–2.6 and local §10. Cassels–Tate adjointness is the imported D7 contract; its application yields the exact isogeny Selmer-ratio and parity statements here.

The general endomorphism rank application assumes a uniform constant `c>0` with `log3#(A_s(F)/ψ_sA_s(F))≥c rank A_s(F)`. Prove the bound from that hypothesis and the factorization into degree-three isogenies. For ψ=[3] it holds with c=1 by finite generation. Do not infer it for every Z[ψ]-module from a degree/exponent ratio. Source: BKLOS Theorem 2.2 and Lemma 9.1, pp. 3 and 12–13; the multiplication-by-three specialization and finite-extension corollary remain unconditional applications of the stated Selmer-mean input.

<a id="support-cohomology"></a>

The EVW input is a uniform homological-stability/Betti estimate for the specified center-free generalized-dihedral Hurwitz spaces: after its degree threshold, Betti numbers are bounded by `C^(i+1)` with C depending on the fixed group, and there is exactly one Frobenius-fixed geometric component in the stated odd-degree, odd-q, `ℓ∤q(q-1)` range. Build the labelled stable hyperelliptic boundary and its compact-type clutching maps; the maps land on the boundary, not in the smooth open stratum. The nodal Picard/normalization exact sequence splits the torsion local system into the required overlapping symplectic summands. Prove the base cases and transvection generation, then lift integral monodromy. The lift from full mod-ℓ image requires g≥2 or ℓ≥5; for g=1,ℓ=3 it additionally requires a nontrivial mod-nine kernel. Source: EVW §§7–8, especially Lemma 8.9, pp. 780–782, with Achter–Pries's monodromy base cases and the integral lifting criterion stated at its target.

Use compact-support duality and weights to sum the lower cohomological traces. For `√q>C≥1` the geometric-series remainder is `C²/(√q-C)`. The top trace counts Frobenius-fixed geometric components, not the total number of components. This gives uniform moments before the upper/lower degree-density argument. Fixed-degree Wood moments instead sum all stable *and boundary* multidegrees, divide by the varying reduced-multiplier torsion `M(q)`, and compare with a finite-valued rational component profile to error `O_n(q^-1/2)`. An ordinary limit exists exactly when that whole profile is eventually constant; a lower bound on stable orthants alone proves a liminf. Sources: EVW Theorem 8.8 and proof, pp. 778–782; Wood Theorems 4.5, 4.7–4.8, pp. 20–25 in arXiv:1702.04644v2.

For de Jong's function-field three-Selmer upper average, construct the locally minimal long-Weierstrass family of exact geometric height d and its automorphism-weighted count. Prove the exact weighted denominator asymptotic `q^(−10d−1)I_d→(1−q^-9)(1−q^-10)/(1−q^-1)>0`. The ternary-cubic surface count bounds the similarly normalized nonidentity numerator by `3/((1−q^-3)(1−q^-2)²(1−q^-1)²)` in limsup. Outside constant j the automorphism order is two; the constant-j count `O(dq^(9d))` and Selmer-dimension bound `C₁d` make its Selmer contribution negligible for sufficiently large fixed q. These facts give the unweighted upper mean `4+O(1/q)`. Source: de Jong, *Counting elliptic surfaces over finite fields*, Theorem 1.2, Propositions 4.12, 4.14, 5.14, 7.5, 7.9 and Lemma 10.2, author DVI pp. 1–2, 8–11, 20, 24–25, 29. Height tends to infinity first. An alternate family still needs a denominator comparison.

The joint enhanced Cohen–Lenstra model is conditional on existence of the finite-level joint-cokernel limits; a positive liminf is sufficient for its zero-cokernel obstruction, but does not establish existence. The polarized-abundance theorem assumes both uniform Rosati-model counting hypotheses, including the real-Weil surface factor. Under those assumptions its repeated-angle atom forces `liminf d_K≥.99` against any spacing law without an atom at zero; a particular GUE distribution is unnecessary for that implication. Source: Lipnowski–Tsimerman, §5, especially Definition 5.16, Lemma 5.11 and the concentration/spacing arguments. For the conjectures over general global fields, specify the short-coefficient family outside characteristics two and three and the long Weierstrass family in those characteristics. Odd/even hyperelliptic degree and Jacobian genus determine which prime laws and shifted two-Selmer laws are conjectured. No coefficient-height conjecture is transferred to a minimal invariant-height Q-family without a denominator comparison.

### Examples

In a split hyperbolic plane there are two quadratic-isotropic lines, even at p=2. Their intersection with a fixed one has dimension zero or one with probability one half. At dimension zero there is one maximal isotropic and its intersection dimension is zero with probability one; no half-parity assertion applies. In a two-dimensional F2 space with quadratic form `x²+xy+y²`, every nonzero vector has value one, although its polar form has isotropic lines. This witnesses why the quadratic condition cannot be dropped.

The symmetric two-by-two matrices over F3 have rank counts `1,8,18`, totaling 27; bordering a fixed rank-r matrix has fibres `3^r`, `2·3^r`, and `3^(n+1)-3^(r+1)` for rank jumps zero, one and two. For p-adic alternating matrices the parity of nullity follows the size, so the two size-parity subsequences must be mixed as specified to get the Poonen–Rains law.

For a prime law with half even and half odd mass, the k-prime common-parity weight is `2^(k-1)∏w_i` for k≥1. At k=0 the carrier is a singleton of mass one; substituting k=0 into the scalar factor would incorrectly give one half. A symplectic rank-zero all-prime model is infinite almost surely, whereas restricting to primes with convergent `Σ1/p` yields a finite group almost surely.

For the Wood profile, if recurring allowed q produce two distinct rational component ratios, the `O_n(q^-1/2)` error tends to zero while the ratios remain separated. Thus the arithmetic normalized moments have different liminf and limsup. Stable-range stars-and-bars counting cannot erase that boundary dependence.

### Dependencies

Layers 0–4; the finite-group moment and matrix tools already constructed in Layer 3; Mathlib probability and projective measures; A2–A3 and A6; SF.2–SF.3 and R09.1; D7 and Selmer L0–L4; Neron normalization/semistable geometry; IG.3–IG.5; EDC.2 and DWP.7; and the explicit local supporting hypotheses above. Conditional arithmetic laws and unproved limit-existence predicates are used only as hypotheses.


## Downstream consumers

AnalyticNumberTheory uses the invariant and local-count interfaces. Field-counting and class-group applications consume the exact isomorphism, embedded and rigid denominators rather than silently change their sampling law. Higher Selmer and twist arguments use the local orbit/Kummer comparison and the proved mean theorems; they do not obtain arbitrary moments from weak convergence. Arithmetic distribution conjectures can be compared to any later proof only after its family, height and local weights have been identified with the predicates defined here.

`Suggested.lean` records representative signatures against the pinned carriers. Its light definitions are `ArithmeticFamily`, `ArithmeticFamily.count`, `ArithmeticFamily.HasRelativeDensity`, `Coefficients.boxHeight`, `Coefficients.monicPolynomial`, `Coefficients.weightedBox`, `Coefficients.binaryValue`, `Coefficients.StrongSquareDivides`, `Coefficients.WeakSquareDivides`, and the invariant, finite matrix and numerical probability definitions it states. The README is the full roadmap: cubic and quartic algebras, quintic resolvents, integral coverings, marked Hurwitz components, Picard torsors, topological quadratic parameter spaces, canonical measures and geometric local systems remain mathematical targets here.
